### How this work is cited

Passages inside Chuanxilu (Instructions for Practical Living) are identified by juan (卷) and item number. The text was assembled by Wang Yangming's disciples after his death and expanded over decades, so a numbered item belongs to a specific juan and edition. Wang's teaching reaches the reader here through his students' compilation rather than through anything he published.

### The work in Wang Yangming’s thought

Wang Yangming (Wang Shouren, 1472–1529) was the Ming Neo-Confucian who taught unity of knowledge and action and innate moral knowing (liangzhi). A statesman and general who suppressed rebellions, he developed teachings in exile and military camps. [More on Wang Yangming](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-yangming) .
